Rayyan memorised faster than anyone else in the Quran circle. He would learn a whole page before the others had learned half of it.

When Sheikh Fouad announced a memorisation competition, Rayyan said to himself, "The prize is mine, no doubt about it."

His friend Anas sat next to him. He was slow at memorising, but he repeated each ayah until it stayed, and he never got bored.

Sometimes Rayyan laughed at him and said, "Are you still on the same page?"

Competition day came, and the boys went up one by one to recite in front of the judges.

Rayyan recited quickly. He stumbled over two ayahs and forgot a word.

Then Anas recited slowly, and did not make a mistake in a single letter.

Rayyan sat watching him, his heart pounding.

When the Sheikh announced the result, he said, "First place: Anas. Second place: Rayyan."

The boys clapped. Anas stood up to receive the prize, and Rayyan sat in his place without moving.

When they came out of the masjid, Rayyan did not congratulate his friend. He walked home alone, with his eyes on the ground.

He said to his father, "I deserved it more. I'm faster than him."

His father said, "Rayyan, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'None of you truly believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself.'"

Then he said, "If you had won, would you have wanted Anas to be happy for you?"

Rayyan was quiet for a long time. Then he remembered Anas repeating the ayah again and again, while he laughed at him.

And he knew that Anas had worked hard to win.

The next day Rayyan came to the circle early. When Anas came in, he got up, hugged him, and said, "Mabruk, Anas — congratulations! You deserve it."

Then he said, "Teach me how you memorise without forgetting."

So the two friends began memorising together: Rayyan going fast, and Anas repeating, until together they memorised better than either of them did alone.

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "None of you truly believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself."

📖 Agreed upon (Al-Bukhari and Muslim). This is a tale told as a parable; it did not happen to anyone in particular.
